note: RESEARCHED amenity sizes, collected 2026-09-20. Federation dimensions are facts and were recorded as numbers only; no drawing, diagram or CAD block was copied. IMPORTANT CONVENTION: for the two racquet sports the footprint below is the PLAYABLE ENCLOSURE (court plus run-off), not the painted court, because the engine's placer only adds CLEARANCE_M = 1.5 m of walking room between facilities and that is not enough run-off to play in. Reserving only the line dimensions would produce an unbuildable court. SOURCES AND STATUS. BADMINTON COURT: BWF Laws of Badminton give the doubles court as exactly 13.4 x 6.1 m (HARD, bwfbadminton.com). The 17.4 x 9.1 m here adds 2.0 m run-off behind each back boundary line and 1.5 m at each side line, the club/recreational figure attributed to Sport England / Badminton England design guidance; that PDF is image-only and could not be read directly, so the run-off is SOFT (consistent secondary sources, not verified against the primary table). BWF guidance for competition asks 2.0 m on all sides, which would make it 17.4 x 10.1 m. TENNIS COURT: ITF Rules of Tennis give the doubles court as exactly 23.77 x 10.97 m (HARD, itftennis.com). 34.8 x 17.1 m is the club/recreational single-court plot (114 ft x 56 ft), consistently cited across tennis-authority sources but not read off the ITF page itself, which returned empty when fetched, so SOFT. ITF tournament standard is larger at about 36.6 x 18.3 m. SWIMMING POOL: no standard governs a residential pool. 25.0 m is chosen because it is the World Aquatics short-course length and the length Indian developers habitually build to; 12.0 m width is the top of the 6-12 m range found in Indian practice. SOFT. Water edge only, coping and deck not included. KIDS POOL: SOFT, no standard; 8.0 x 5.0 m is the top of the 6x4 to 8x5 m range found in Indian practice; toddler depth 0.3-0.6 m. CRICKET PRACTICE NET: SOFT. No BCCI or ICC published dimension standard was found, which is itself worth knowing. One lane at 25.0 x 3.6 m sits inside the 20-27 m x 3.0-3.6 m range in general sports-facility design practice; a cricket pitch is 20.12 m stump to stump and a net lane is built longer to allow a run-up. CHILDRENS PLAY: SOFT as a footprint. 12.0 x 10.0 m = 120 sqm sits inside the 50-150 sqm typical for Indian projects. The REQUIREMENT is hard: Telangana rule 7(a)(vii) names a tot lot as a use of the mandatory organized open space, which is why counts_as_open_space is true. No Indian rule giving a minimum tot-lot AREA was found. FITNESS / YOGA DECK: SOFT, no standard. 12.0 x 7.0 m = 84 sqm at roughly 4.5 sqm per person outdoors suits about 18 people. counts_as_open_space is FALSE because a paved deck is not greenery, tot lot or soft landscaping under rule 7(a)(vii). SENIORS SEATING: SOFT and the weakest number here. No standards body and no consistent developer convention publishes a footprint; 8.0 x 6.0 m is a working assumption only. counts_as_open_space is true because seating in landscape is a soft use. SECURITY CABIN: SOFT, no standard. 2.4 x 2.4 m is the largest standard Indian prefab guard cabin (8x8 ft), suitable for two guards with a shift seat; many projects build a larger masonry gate house, so the firm should override this. JOGGING TRACK: requested but NOT INCLUDED AS AN ITEM, on purpose. A jogging track is a loop around the site, and this schema can only express an axis-aligned rectangle, so adding it would make the placer reserve a solid block of land that is not what a track is. The number for when the engine gains a track: 1.2 to 2.0 m wide for a compact single-file internal path, and 2.5 to 3.5 m where joggers and walkers share one loop. Sources genuinely disagree, so it is a range, not a number. For reference World Athletics Technical Rule C2.1 fixes a competition running lane at 1.22 m, but that is a track-and-field fact, not a residential standard. EVERY SOFT NUMBER IS A STARTING POINT FOR THE FIRM TO OVERRIDE PER PROJECT.
